chunks: He who keeps his secret among you is the same to Him as he who speaks out publicly, and he who hides himself in the night and walks freely in the day.

key_terms.جَهَرَ: to make public or speak aloud
key_terms.سَارِبٌ: one who walks freely or moves about openly
key_terms.مُسْتَخْفٍ: one who hides or conceals himself

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the secret and the public speech are equal in the eyes of Allah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the completeness of Allah's knowledge (Ilm al-Ghayb), affirming that no layer of concealment—whether in speech or action, day or night—can escape His awareness. It serves as a reminder of divine accountability (Hisab), where internal intentions and external actions are equally scrutinized, reinforcing the concept of 'Alam al-Mithal' where the spiritual reality mirrors the physical. This assurance of omniscience encourages believers to maintain sincerity (Ikhlas) in both private devotion and public conduct.
